note: **2 South Road, schedule 235 of the 1939 Register.** The property had stood in the list with no census in any round. A. Hagues reads the household off the page: three women, no head, and one name the index gives two ways - which A. Hagues settles: the amending hand rewrote the forename along with the surname, so the odd forename in the index is the clerk's, not hers.
source: 1939 Register, South Road run, schedules 229 to 237

census.source: 1939 Register, schedule 235, 2 South Road - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 1; this schedule belongs to the South Road and Cavendish Crescent South run, numbered 229 to 237, and not to the RMGC book; sub number 1 and married, with a parlourmaid and a cook under her - her husband is not on the page

1939 Register, schedule 235, 2 South Road - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 2; this schedule belongs to the South Road and Cavendish Crescent South run, numbered 229 to 237, and not to the RMGC book

1939 Register, schedule 235, 2 South Road - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 3; this schedule belongs to the South Road and Cavendish Crescent South run, numbered 229 to 237, and not to the RMGC book; the index gives her as Acho (Victoria) Wright (Richardson). She was Victoria throughout: the hand that wrote the married surname over Richardson rewrote the forename with it, which is what Acho is - not a name she was ever called. Entered as Victoria Richardson, her name on the night, with Victoria Wright kept as the married name
